name: pyupgrade-selective-rewrite-suppression-8893
instr:
pyupgrade cannot suppress individual rewrites from source comments while continuing unrelated safe modernizations. Support same-line and nested disable/enable scopes and single-use disable-next scopes across logical statements and multiline syntax.

Directives use `# pyupgrade: disable=<rules>`, `# pyupgrade: enable=<rules>`, and `# pyupgrade: disable-next=<rules>`, where `<rules>` is one rule name or a comma-separated list; an empty entry is malformed. `available_rules` returns each unique name once, sorted by name. `DirectiveKind` is an Enum. Resolve nested scopes deterministically per candidate. Disable-next covers exactly the next complete statement, including decorators, then expires. Valid directive comments remain unchanged.

Suppression preserves the complete source spelling changed by the named rewrite. Nested, adjacent, and mixed candidates follow their own names and innermost applicable scopes while sharing boundaries. A suppressed outer literal or call does not block eligible nested candidates. For typing unions, include the complete annotation subscription, including multiline commas, parentheses, and quoted arguments.

Apply suppression to set literals, typing unions, dot-format and percent-format modernization, import alias and statement changes, subprocess calls, defaultdict lambdas, and lexical rewrites, preserving distinct safety exclusions. Filter only otherwise eligible candidates; unsafe candidates remain recognized as no-ops. AST-driven and lexical trans
